member.name: T:SafeName.ErrorReason
member.summary: The reason a name or path failed validation. Each carries one.

member.name: F:SafeName.ErrorReason.Empty
member.summary: The name is null, empty, all whitespace, or resolves to nothing after removing trailing dots and spaces (for example "." or "..").

member.name: F:SafeName.ErrorReason.ReservedCharacter
member.summary: The name contains a character reserved by the target platform, such as < > : " | ? * on Windows.

member.name: F:SafeName.ErrorReason.ControlCharacter
member.summary: The name contains a control character (including NUL and DEL).

member.name: F:SafeName.ErrorReason.ReservedDeviceName
member.summary: The name is, or begins with, a Windows reserved device name such as CON or COM1. These are reserved even when they carry an extension (CON.txt).

member.name: F:SafeName.ErrorReason.TrailingDotOrSpace
member.summary: The name ends with a dot or a space. Windows silently strips these, which breaks round-tripping (a saved "report." is read back as "report").

member.name: F:SafeName.ErrorReason.TooLong
member.summary: The name or path exceeds the configured maximum length.

member.name: F:SafeName.ErrorReason.PathSeparatorPresent
member.summary: A filename component contains a path separator (/ on POSIX; / or \ on Windows). A single component must never span directories.

member.name: F:SafeName.ErrorReason.PathTraversal
member.summary: A path contains a traversal segment (..) or a current-directory segment (.) that could escape or confuse the intended location.

member.name: F:SafeName.ErrorReason.UnpairedSurrogate
member.summary: The name contains an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate (a high surrogate not followed by a low, or a low surrogate not preceded by a high). Such a string is not valid Unicode and cannot be encoded to UTF-8 without loss.

member.name: T:SafeName.FilePath
member.summary: Sanitizes and validates a full, multi-segment path: it splits on separators, cleans each segment as a filename, neutralizes traversal, and rejoins with the platform separator.

remarks.para: This makes the names in a path safe. It is not a substitute for confining filesystem access to a base directory. Traversal segments (..) are stripped, but if you then combine the result with a base path you must still resolve and check containment yourself; see the README security section for the Path.GetFullPath pattern.
All members are static and thread-safe.

Each segment is sanitized as a filename, . and .. segments are removed, drive letters and UNC and absolute roots are preserved, the segments are rejoined with the platform separator, and the whole result is truncated to the maximum path length. Never throws on .
member.param: The candidate path. May be null, empty, absolute, relative, or hostile.
Path sanitization options, or for the defaults.

member.summary: Returns whether is a Windows reserved device name. The stem (the part before the first dot, with trailing spaces removed) is compared case-insensitively, so CON, con, CON.txt, and CON.tar.gz are all reserved, while CONtext and COM0 are not.

member.name: T:SafeName.MaxLengthUnit
member.summary: The unit in which a maximum length is measured and enforced.
member.remarks: This choice is easy to get wrong and matters. Most Unix filesystems (ext4, APFS, XFS) limit a filename component to 255 bytes, and they store names as UTF-8, so a name of 100 emoji is 400 bytes and is rejected even though it is only 100 characters. NTFS limits to 255 UTF-16 code units. Because the byte limit is the stricter and more portable one, is the default.

member.name: F:SafeName.MaxLengthUnit.Utf8Bytes
member.summary: Measure length as the number of UTF-8 bytes. This is the default and matches how ext4, APFS, and most Unix filesystems enforce their 255-limit.

member.name: F:SafeName.MaxLengthUnit.Chars
member.summary: Measure length as the number of UTF-16 code units (the value of ). This matches how NTFS enforces its 255-limit.

member.name: T:SafeName.PlatformProfile
member.summary: Selects the set of filesystem rules used when sanitizing or validating a name.
member.remarks: The rules a name must satisfy differ between operating systems. A profile picks which rule set to apply. Unless you know the target filesystem, prefer , which forbids anything forbidden on either Windows or POSIX and so produces names that are safe on both.

member.name: F:SafeName.PlatformProfile.Windows
member.summary: Windows (NTFS/FAT) rules: forbids the characters < > : " / \ | ? * and all control characters, the reserved device names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-COM9, LPT1-LPT9, even with an extension), and trailing dots and spaces.

member.name: F:SafeName.PlatformProfile.Posix
member.summary: POSIX (Linux, macOS, and most Unix filesystems) rules: forbids only the forward slash and the NUL character in a filename component. Trailing dots and spaces, control characters other than NUL, and the Windows reserved device names are all permitted.

member.name: F:SafeName.PlatformProfile.Universal
member.summary: The intersection of the Windows and POSIX rules: a name is only valid if it is valid on both. This is the default and is the correct choice when you do not control the target filesystem (cross-platform apps, cloud sync, archives, uploads that may be restored anywhere).

member.name: F:SafeName.PlatformProfile.Auto
member.summary: Detects the current operating system at call time and applies on Windows or elsewhere.
